results.content:
President Trump's standing kept sliding by nearly every measure this week, though pollsters do not agree by how much. A Civiqs tracker put his approval at 34 per cent as of September 4; a Focaldata/Financial Times poll fielded through September 2 put it at 32 per cent, its lowest reading since that tracker began in May, with just 17 per cent approving of his handling of inflation and the cost of living. Nationally, 35 percent of voters approve of Trump's job performance while 59 percent disapprove as of August 19, leaving him significantly underwater with a net approval rating of -24, according to Civiqs' rolling online tracking poll of registered voters. The survey has garnered 124,759 responses since January 20, 2025, when Trump was inaugurated for a second term. Nationally, Trump stands at 34 percent approval and 60 percent disapproval, giving him a net approval rating of minus 26.
